#1922. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”

“We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

Man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier

And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”

“It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”

“They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”

A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm

📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

#1921. England's Harry Kane wants his next Wembley trophy to be in the Euro 2028 final

Thursday was Kane's night at England's spiritual home as he made a goal then scored his 92nd for his country on the occasion of his record-breaking 126th cap for the Three Lions.

But it was also an opportunity to mark him becoming the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or – the annual prize for the best European-based footballer and de facto, best player in the world.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Kane received it at a ceremony in London last month, and was presented with it before his club Bayern Munich's game against Borussia Dortmund, but it was important to him to do it again on international duty.

And it made him dream of captaining England to a first major trophy since 1966 when the European Championship final returns to Wembley in 2028.

"I think the crowd would be a bit more crazy if we're lifting the Euro 2028 trophy, that's for sure," said Kane. "But it inspired me.

"To be able to share the Ballon d'Or with our fans is important because we haven't won it for a long time.

"Not just the 126 (caps), but also the Ballon d'Or is an important occasion to mark.

"I know if we win a major tournament, which is my ultimate goal in my career, with England, then the celebration, not just in the stadium, but around the whole country, will be especially beautiful with it.

"I don't think I need any more motivation to make it happen, but it'll be incredible if we can."

Kane admitted on Thursday the enormity of what he has achieved this season has not yet hit him.

"The reception that I've had has been overwhelming and incredible," he said.

"I don't know if any of this has sunk in yet. Maybe in the (Bundesliga's) winter break, when I've got a couple of weeks off, I'll go on a beach somewhere and try and reflect on everything.

"Whether I'll be able to do that through my career, I'm not so sure. I'm so focused on just the next thing and the next moment.

"So if I've fully taken everything that I've achieved these last couple of weeks, I'm not quite sure. Ultimately, it's about the next thing. It's about Sunday (when England play Spain in a game to decide who tops their Nations League group), then it's about club football again.

"Hopefully over the Christmas break I'll have a good drink with my wife and take it all in."

#1920. “I just want to play” – Endrick fuels Real Madrid exit talk amid AC Milan links

Endrick has not closed the door on the idea of leaving Real Madrid as he continues to be linked with a move to AC Milan.

It is no secret that Milan tried to sign Endrick on a loan deal in the summer window, but Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho blocked his exit. After getting not much playing time in the first part of the season, talk has grown that the Brazilian could be allowed to depart in January.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Milan remain at the window as they look to strengthen their attack with an added goal threat, while Roma have also been linked, as have clubs in the Premier League. Fabrizio Romano even reported that the former Palmeiras star is an ‘obsession’ for Gerry Cardinale.

Interviewed by Globo’s Cahe Mota directly from the Brazilian national team’s training camp, Endrick commented on his future and seemed to offer a bit of hope to interested clubs.

“I’m only 20 years old, so I’ll see how things unfold. I just want to play, be happy, and help my team-mates. I don’t know what will happen in January; it’s all in God’s hands. I just ask for what’s best for my career,” he said (via MilanNews).

“Whatever happens, will happen. I’ll keep my feet on the ground and give my all. Madrid is a wonderful city, but I’ll always do whatever it takes to keep growing and moving forward in my career.”

#1919. Why England's Thomas Tuchel is right to talk up Spain 'final'

In reality, it is nothing of the sort. All that will be at stake at kick-off in the Metropolitano Stadium at 7.45pm is who wins Nations League A Group 3, and gets a home second leg in March's quarter-finals, but it makes sense for the coach to big it up.

Because if anything, England find matches between tournaments too easy. They qualified for the last World Cup without conceding a goal, yet found it hard work in America and Mexico.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Nations League is supposed to match equals, yet they ran out 7-0 winners in Croatia in October. That Thursday's 2-1 win in the reverse game was much tighter was cause for celebration with Tuchel.

"Because we didn't take our chances it was a tight match, which is good overall," he reflected, “because it can't always be glamorous and super-exciting. Sometimes it's about being serious and determined.

"We wanted a final, and on Sunday in Spain we have it."

Tuchel might rest the man he says is still his first-choice goalkeeper, Jordan Pickford, to give Leeds United's James Trafford another chance, slightly undermining his billing of the game.

But Trafford is getting his chance because he is performing so well and other changes will be more likely to strengthen England, with Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence likely to be available after injury and Miles Lewis-Skelly having served a one-match ban.

The narrative around this generation of England players is that they are flat-track bullies, brilliant in qualifying but flaky in finals and semi-finals, or whenever they come up against the world's elite.

World and European champions Spain won 3-2 at Wembley in September, so only need a draw.

They beat England in the last European Championship final, the second in a row the Three Lions had been tamed in. They lost this year's World Cup semi-final to Argentina and started the nearly-men cycle with a last-four defeat to Croatia in 2018.

When they got to the Nations League semi-finals in 2019, poor defending by John Stones and Kyle Walker saw them lose 3-1 to the Netherlands in extra-time.

So no, Sunday is not a "final", a huge occasion, a do-or-die moment for Tuchel's team. But it will not do them any harm to think so.

#1918. Mauricio Pochettino tipped to sign Real Madrid defender for Manchester United

Mauricio Pochettino has been tipped to sign Real Madrid defender and former Chelsea star Antonio Rudiger for Manchester United.

Pochettino is set to take charge at Old Trafford and replace Michael Carrick, who will be sacked following a dismal start to the season.

United are just 18th in the Premier League after ten games – their lowest position at this stage of a campaign since 1986.

Old Trafford bosses held a review into Carrick’s position earlier this week and appear to have decided to make a change in the dugout.

Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Unai Emery, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann have all been linked with the Manchester United job in recent weeks.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But United chose Pochettino as their first-choice pick this week and are currently finalising a deal to bring the Argentine back to the Premier League.

Pochettino, who will step down from his role as head coach of the USA to take over at Manchester United, has already worked at fellow English clubs Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, as well as Spanish side Espanyol and French giants PSG.

One of the biggest problems for United this season has been a fragile defence and ex-Premier League striker Charlie Austin insists Pochettino ‘needs a whole new back-four’.

Austin believes Pochettino could look to sign someone like Rudiger, the Real Madrid and Germany centre-back who previously spent five years in England with Chelsea.

#1917. Harry Kane on the inspiration to keep on shining for England

Thursday night at Wembley was not about England v Croatia, not really. It was not particularly about the Nations League, where the hosts needed to avoid a seven-goal defeat to be sure of going through to the quarter-finals (ooh the jeopardy!). It was all about Kane.

England's captain was greeted with a huge tifo as he led his team out of the tunnel for the 98th time.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Before the anthems and handshakes he broke from the line to pick his Ballon d'Or trophy off a plinth, and be presented with a framed shirt to mark his 126th appearance for the Three Lions, a new record.

Luka Modric handed him a replica of Croatia's oldest preserved football, brought to Zupanja by English industrialists in 1880.

It was a nice touch between two teams who have got to know each other rather well in the 21st Century, and two players who were team-mates at Tottenham Hotspur.

Modric is 41 years-old, eight years his senior. When he was 33, Modric also won the Ballon d'Or but it has not sated his appetite.

He was only a substitute when he won his 207th Croatia cap on Thursday, but it was telling he was given a warm ovation when he came off the bench in the second half with the game still in the balance.

Few opposing players get that at Wembley, and it was in stark contrast to the reception afforded to former Leeds United loanee Ben White when he came off the home bench two minutes later. He has not been forgiven for abandoning the ship at the 2022 winter World Cup.

Modric plays his club football at AC Milan, where there is a proud history of elderly players thriving, and has contributed nearly 750 Serie A minutes already this season.

Kane seems to be getting better, a more rounded player with every year of his 30s.

His part in the first goal was a case in point. The younger Kane did not often drop deep and play passes of the quality that released Jude Bellingham to set up Morgan Rogers for England's opener in the 2-1 win, but the 2026 version spends more time away from the frontline than on it.

"That's an area of the pitch I like to play in, that kind of left pocket," he explained. "The more I play with the guys, the more of a relationship I build up with Jude and Morgan and Trent (Alexander-Arnold, selected at right-back), whoever's playing, they know when I'm in that position, I'm probably going to play that type of ball, so they make the runs.

"It's just a pass that's a big strength of mine. It's something I've practised a lot when I was young and still do. You've seen over recent years, especially, that it's been a big weapon."

To carry on as long as Modric is a big ask but Kane has plenty of incentive to go on a couple more years yet.

His penalty to win the game five minutes after sloppy England set-piece defending brought Croatia back into it with a Petar Sucic strike was his 92nd goal for his country.

Only three other players – Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Iran's Ali Daei – have hit 100 in international football but there was no dodging the question when he was asked if it was possible: "I think it's achievable for sure."

And with the talent around him, leading his team onto the winner's podium at the 2028 European Championship final at Wembley, after consecutive losing finals, looks realistic too.

"If we win a major tournament, which is my ultimate goal, the celebrations not just inside the stadium, will be incredible," he said.

Seeing someone like you achieve what you want to is perhaps the biggest motivation of all.

"He's an inspiration for all of us," marvelled Kane when asked about Modric. "What an incredible player, what a great person as well, and someone who's looked after himself, a great professional.

"To be playing at 41 now, still at this level, is a credit to all of his hard work and his mentality. That inspires me to push to the limits.

"I think you just keep going to see how far your body takes you, your mentality takes you.

"As long as I feel like I can help the national team, as long as I feel like I'm performing at the highest level, I'll be here. Whether that's until I'm 40 we'll have to wait and see.

Thursday was just about celebrating one of the England greats and having failed to score and even missed a penalty since being crowned European football’s best player, he did not disappoint.

"It's demanding to get all the recognition, all the prizes, all the acknowledgement,” said Kane’s coach, Thomas Tuchel. “The gentleman he is, he responds to everything.

"It would be easy to lose focus, which he obviously never does.

"We were determined to get this result on his special evening. That he got it in the end with a decisive penalty makes it even more perfect.”

England won 7-0 in Croatia in October. Kane made Thursday top it.

#1916. Man Utd interested in £75m Chelsea star ahead of January transfer window

Manchester United are reportedly weighing up an ambitious bid for out-of-favour Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto.

There were high hopes for Gusto when Chelsea signed the then 19-year-old for a fee of £30.7million from Lyon back in January 2023, when Graham Potter was in charge.

Gusto, now 23, has gone on to make a total of 144 appearances in all competitions for the Blues while helping the club win the Europa Conference League and the Club World Cup.

However, for the most part, Gusto has been forced to compete for minutes with Reece James when the Chelsea captain has been fit, meaning he has often struggled to get a consistent run of games under his belt.

James’ latest injury, likely to keep the Englishman sidelined until the New Year, had appeared to have opened the door for Gusto to nail down regular playing time under new head coach Xabi Alonso.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Gusto has not started a match in the Premier League since as far back as September, though, with Josh Acheampong seemingly overtaking the France international in the pecking order at Stamford Bridge.

Widespread reports earlier this week indicated Gusto was ‘assessing his options’ and ‘open’ to the prospect of leaving Chelsea in search of a fresh challenge elsewhere.

According to talkSPORT, this has put both Manchester clubs on red alert, with United and City said to be ‘interested’ and ‘keeping tabs’ on the situation should an opportunity arise.

It’s claimed it may take an offer in the region of £75million to convince Chelsea to part with Gusto.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It remains to be seen if either United or City will make a formal approach to prise the former Lyon man away from west London this winter.

City’s rumoured pursuit of Gusto stretches back for some time, with Enzo Maresca understood to have been keen on a reunion with the full-back when he took over the reins at the Etihad in the summer.

Gusto has three-and-a-half years remaining on his current contract with Chelsea.

There are, of course, complications for both United and City when it comes to potential transfer dealings this January, with the former reportedly on the verge of a managerial change and the latter still yet to learn their punishment for Premier League rule breaches.

Gusto filled in as a makeshift midfielder during Moises Caicedo’s absence from the team through injury and there were some suggestions the Frenchman could continue in the role under Alonso.

But speaking exclusively to Metro at the time, ex-Chelsea midfielder Gus Poyet insisted Gusto should look to earn Alonso’s trust by becoming the best possible right-back.

‘I do remember one of the most impressive decisions by a coach – Pep Guardiola at Bayern Munich, playing Lahm as a central midfielder,’ Poyet explained.

‘It was big news at the time, because he had the quality. Chelsea have been doing this with Reece James, because they understand it’s a possibility. Now Gusto as well.

‘But any right-back becoming a good central midfielder? No chance. Because full-backs naturally get used to playing with the line next to them, either on their right side or their left. Nobody’s coming at them from that side, because you’ve got the line.

‘Now, when you play in the middle, players come at you from everywhere, and not every player is the same. So yes, for one game [they can play there]. Yes, for twenty minutes. Not constantly. And now we see Chelsea playing a right-back as a central midfielder every game.

‘This is Chelsea — we’re not talking about a fourth-division club with no possibility of bringing in a player. So yes, it’s a little bit strange. And I don’t think it’s ideal.’

#1915. Xabi Alonso must look at HIMSELF, not the officials, as another questionable line-up sees Chelsea fold at Sunderland - and Cole Palmer wastes his chance to respond to Thomas Tuchel snub, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 11:14 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 17:34 EST, 8 November 2026

When searching for why Chelsea were beaten by the side who were sitting bottom of the Premier League, the temptation from Xabi Alonso might be to describe this defeat as a tale of two penalties.

First, Chelsea were denied one when Cole Palmer was sandwiched by Luke O'Nien and Jules Ahoka as he entered the Sunderland area, with the officials concluding the contact occurred outside of the box.

Then, Sunderland were awarded one when Brian Brobbey was brought down by Levi Colwill. The striker had hold of the defender at the same time, and arguably clipped his own heel upon second viewing, but Enzo Le Fee gladly accepted the opportunity to score the game's only goal.

However, it would be wrong to blame this deserved defeat on those two decisions alone. Referee Jarred Gillett and VAR Nick Hopton were weak but not the reason that Chelsea lost.

This was actually a tale of two strikers. Sunderland had one in the brilliant bully that is Brobbey, whereas Chelsea had nobody after Alonso yet again decided against starting Danny Welbeck.

In the three Premier League games played since Joao Pedro's injury – against Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and now Sunderland – Alonso has gone with Morgan Rogers as a false nine once and Pedro Neto twice. Welbeck was on the bench in all of those matches.

Sunderland handed Chelsea a brutal reality check as they climbed off the foot of the table

The visitors fell victim to two questionable penalty calls at the Stadium of Light

We are not saying the 35-year-old is the answer to all of Alonso's problems, but he is an actual No9 who scored 13 times in the Premier League for Brighton last season.

Neto was hardly going to have a high success rate when wrestling with centre backs for the long balls which were coming from Colwill and Co. It is a question that needs asking, therefore, especially after another loss.

Why did Chelsea sign Welbeck if not to play when Joao Pedro is injured?

Welbeck came on in the 62nd minute here, but by then, a familiar feeling was washing over Chelsea.

They lost 2-1 here at the very end of last season. Malo Gusto scored an own goal, Wesley Fofana was red carded, and Chelsea, managed by Calum McFarlane in the interim, failed to qualify for any form of European football.

They smacked of an utterly unserious side then, and resembled it here, too.

Chelsea had a week to prepare for this Premier League clash while Sunderland were playing – and losing – to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League.

Regis Le Bris' side had not won in the league since August. Yet they were the sharper of the two teams here.

It hardly helped Alonso that Chelsea's attackers never appeared at it individually.

Cole Palmer had a stinker. This was supposed to be an opportunity to show why Thomas Tuchel made a mistake in not naming him in his latest England squad. If anything, he helped make sure those accusations cannot be levelled at Tuchel over this break.

Xabi Alonso tinkered with his line-up and it failed to pay off in a second defeat in three games

Cole Palmer had a stinker in a woeful response to Thomas Tuchel's England snub

Rogers' performance was best summed up by the time he simply sprinted out of play with the ball to gift Sunderland a goal-kick. He and Palmer resembled no-shows.

Sunderland (4-2-3-1): Roefs 6; Hume 7, Mukiele 7, O'Nien 6, Mandava 7; Xhaka 6 (Ahoka 4, 6), Sadiki 7; Meunier 6, Talbi 6 (Rigg 88), Le Fee 6 (Angulo 88); Brobbey 8 (Isidor 67, 6)

Subs (not used): Ellborg, Danso, Methalie, Fofana, Tutierov

Booked: Ahoka, Meunier, Brobbey, O'Nien, Angulo

Chelsea (4-3-3): Penders 6; Palestra 5 (Gusto 62, 5), Fofana 5, Colwill 4 (Estevao 45, 6), Chavarria 5 (Quenda 79); Caicedo 6, Lavia 6, Henderson 6 (Emegha 87); Palmer 4, Neto 5 (Welbeck 62, 5), Rogers 4

Subs (not used): Sharman-Lowe, Barco, Anselmino, Nicoll-Jazuli

Neto looked like a lost little boy trying to lead Chelsea's line in the absence of Joao Pedro.

The half-time statistics said Chelsea had sent more open-play crosses into Sunderland's box in the opening 45 minutes than in their entire games v Fulham, Everton, Tottenham, Manchester United, Bournemouth and Brighton.

Except, they had no striker for Alonso's full backs Marco Palestra or Pep Chavarria to try to find. Just 5ft 8in Neto and the odd other box-crasher.

Trailing 1-0 at half-time here, Alonso made a singular substitution. It was to introduce Estevao for Colwill, who had been tormented by Brobbey.

Le Bris was asked in his post-match press conference if there is another player like his striker in the Premier League. He thought long and hard before answering: 'What do you think? I don't think so. His physicality, his intensity, it's impressive, that's for sure. The build-up is so important to have a target man.'

Alonso chipped in on Brobbey: 'He is not unstoppable. He is stoppable but only when you defend better than we did.' On his own attack, he added: 'We didn't produce enough to deserve to win.'

Sunderland's tactic of hoofing the ball up to Brobbey worked wonders. He scared the daylights out of Chelsea's centre backs. When Fofana first arrived at the Stadium of Light, a Chelsea fan shouted at him as he got off the bus. 'Fofana, please be on the bench,' he said. Fofana may have been wishing he was a substitute as well whenever he was wrestling with Brobbey.

It was the long-ball approach which led to Sunderland winning their penalty. They smashed it towards the top of the pitch and Brobbey bullied Colwill. Sunderland won their spot-kick and, in truth, deserved the lead for the sheer energy they brought to this match.

Alonso is ten Premier League games into his Chelsea career. The honeymoon period is over. Sunderland lost their captain Granit Xhaka to an injury after two minutes here. Chelsea had named a line-up featuring three midfielders. But they never showed any signs of control, and for that, Alonso should be looking at himself and his own side rather than the refereeing team.

#1914. Man Utd sack Michael Carrick and provide update on Mauricio Pochettino arrival

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed their new head coach.

Carrick led training at Carrington this week despite it becoming clear a change was imminent as early as Monday evening.

He arrived at United’s training base at Carrington just before 8am on Thursday morning, leaving less than two-and-a-half hours later having been relieved of his duties.

Behind the scenes, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have sought approval from minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to part ways with Carrick, with a deal for Pochettino, currently serving as the USA men’s head coach, in place.

Carrick has been on the brink at various stages this season with United sat in the relegation zone in 18th place after 10 games, winning just once against newly promoted Ipswich Town.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

United opted against making a change during the international break in September and October when Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe were the leading contenders for the job.

Carrick gave himself a lifeline as United came from behind to beat Roma in the Champions League at the start of the month. United also fought back twice from 2-1 down in the same game against Aston Villa on Sunday to rescue a 4-4 draw but the decision was made the following day to part ways with the former midfielder.

His staff are also expected to leave, including former defender Jonny Evans who was pictured leaving Carrington with his belongings on Wednesday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Carrick’s departure marks the third season in a row United have sacked a manager midway through the campaign.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Pochettino’s first game in charge is expected to be the visit to Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

Carrick, who had a brief spell as interim boss in 2021, took the reins again in January following Ruben Amorim’s dismissal, securing hugely impressive wins over Manchester City and Arsenal in his opening two games.

They won 12 of their 17 games during the second-half of the 2025-26 season, securing third place and Champions League qualification with a game to spare. United picked up more points than champions Arsenal managed in the period from Carrick’s game in charge until the end of the campaign.

United clearly benefited from the lighter schedule in that run with just the Premier League to focus on. With European football back on the menu this season, reinforcements were needed.

United signed three new midfielders in the summer in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba but missed out on their top targets Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes who joined Manchester City and Tottenham respectively.

The club also failed to sign another left-back and a striker – positions they were in desperate need of cover for. United are paying the price now with Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko injured.

Before the comeback victory over Roma, United’s only wins this season came at home to Ipswich and against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah. Following a particularly harrowing defeat to Como in the Champions League, club captain Bruno Fernandes publicly challenged the manager’s tactics with the skipper dropped for the subsequent game against Chelsea.

Following the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, Carrick was applauded off the pitch by supporters who instead turned their ire towards the players in a clear picture of where the frustration lies.

#1913. 'I have a letter from a nine-year-old fan on my cupboard door' - Sheffield United's Amy Andrews motivated by taking unconventional route

There is no lip service being paid, on whatever side of the barrier you stand. Amy Andrews was one of those girls who leant across in her youth, now it is she who makes a few memories for the smiling faces of the young Sheffield United fans that greet her at Bramall Lane.

“You don't realise who's there waiting for you, there could be a child that's been waiting for so long to meet you and for you to just sign something and have a photo with them and it means the world,” says the 26-year-old forward who is in her second year with the Blades in WSL2.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“We have the opportunity to give back to our fans that spend money and time coming to watch us. We get letters from the fans. I had one from a nine-year-old that I've stuck on my cupboard door. I look at it every day and it motivates me.”

Her own story is an inspirational one. Andrews didn’t get into professional football via the now conventional route through an elite club academy.

She had to go to America to find her path after two club academies near her Birmingham home chewed her up and spat her out.

“I felt like we weren't really cared for,” laments Andrews. “It made me quit the game for a year and then I went back to my local club with my best friends because I just wanted to enjoy my football again.

“Then America came up and that's how I got here, I had to take the harder route, I've been fighting against opinions and a different background all my life.

“There's kids now that have got Nike deals who are assigned to WSL teams but haven't played in the WSL.

“Going to America (she attended Western Illinois) shaped me to be the player and person I am today, because you just learn so much, leaving home at 18. It was quite difficult at first but I got used to it in the end, and I'd do it again if I could and would definitely recommend it.”

When she returned home she had spells in the second tier with Durham Cestria and Newcastle United. But after falling out of favour at Newcastle when new investment came in, Sheffield United offered her a fresh start in July 2025.

“When I met with the coaching staff and analysts, they valued me a lot, they showed me clips of me playing and how they're going to bring that out of me,” says Andrews.

“I just thought I need to get a hard-working club that's going to play me and value me.”

She has found her home in Sheffield. Andrews scored 10 goals last season - “United helped me rediscover my confidence” - and bagged her first hat-trick against former club Durham at Bramall Lane in September.

“That’s something I’ve had on my list of goals since I've turned professional, so it meant a lot,” she beams. “But I immediately turned my thoughts to when can I get my next one.”

It may happen on Saturday night against Bristol City at Bramall Lane, a showcase game for which adult tickets are £10, concessions £5.

“The pitch at Bramall Lane is so smooth, like a carpet,” she says.

“It's a privilege to play there. I remember playing for Newcastle at St James’ Park against AC Milan, scoring the equaliser in the last minute and then a penalty in the penalty shoot-out; that was unbelievable. I played there when there were 38,000 fans - amazing

“It gave me a taster of what I want to achieve. I know I'm good enough to get to the WSL. There's no point playing football if you don't have those goals, because what are you fighting for?

“I never got that opportunity to take the conventional route when I was growing up, so that's what I'm striving for. That's what motivates me.

“I feel like the odd one out. I'm so hungry to prove people wrong. I want people to hear my story.

#1912. Expected Points and clinical shooting: Stats highlight worries about sustainability of Milan’s Serie A form

AC Milan have collected more points than they deserved so far in the 2026-27 Serie A season, according to statistical data.

As MilanPress write, the Expected Points ranking makes for worrying reading. The metric compares the points actually earned by Serie A teams with those expected based on performances and chances created and conceded in the first 11 rounds of the league season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri have earned 24 points compared to approximately 17 expected, meaning they are ‘over-performing’ by seven points. Milan are currently fourth in the table behind Lazio, Inter and Roma, but they should be a few places lower.

Inter are second with 28 actual points, but should have collected around 26, while Juventus are on 18 points earned versus the expected 21. Napoli also obtained less than the data indicated they should have, with 15 actual points compared to the approximately 19 expected.

The numbers, therefore, reveal a Milan that is particularly effective in turning its performances into tangible results. This is a positive aspect in terms of the league table, but also food for thought. Is it sustainable moving forwards?

Another interesting statistic has come from Kickest, which perhaps highlights why Ruben Amorim’s side have been able to out-perform what the data suggests.

They reveal that there are 113 players with at least 10 shots in Serie A so far in 2026-27. The top four with the best conversion rates have something in common: they play for the Diavolo.

➤ Rabiot — 41.7% (5 goals) ➤ Moreira — 40.0% (4) ➤ Cisse — 38.5% (5) ➤ Pulisic — 36.4% (4) ➤ De Bruyne — 30.0% (3)

It is reminiscent of something we published in January, when the shooting numbers under Massimiliano Allegri were similarly remarkable. As we know, a late-season collapse ended up coming.

Then there was the revelation from Sky after the Genoa game, as they looked at data per 30 minutes of possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. So, Milan must get much better at generating and sustaining pressure, or the results might start to regress.

‘The summer, maybe the winter as well, the transfer window is going to be the players that he wants,’ said the former defender.

‘Also the facilities are going to be built also to the things that he wants. Making players fit, food-wise, gym-wise, everything needs to be how he wants it, that’s a big part of his philosophy.

‘Then he’ll want to buy the players. Maybe not always the biggest names, biggest talents, but guys with desire to win, desire to become better, desire to run. I think if you see the players he bought for Spurs, that’s thing number one, the desire to become better, the desire to win games, wins duels, to run.

‘That’s why I think Pochettino is the man for Man United, to change things around. In the past couple of transfer windows they’ve bought good players, good quality but they miss some chemistry, they miss the intensity and I think Pochettino will bring that.

‘He brings the mentality. If you work hard and bring your A game every single day, everything you want you can achieve. He will bring intensity and the mindset will change at Man United.’

#1910. Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

That goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

That confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

While they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

Had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

Considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

Johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

That was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

Will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

Mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

It’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

Chelsea have been better this half than the first 45, they’ve been able to control the pace of the game well since the break.

The pace has slowed down since the break, Chelsea seeing more of the ball. They work it right before Watson loses possession on the edge of the area.

The referee clearly forgot about the hydration break and the two teams are having a belated one now. Delightful...

I reckon there’s another goal left in this match. It’s been entertaining fare and the hosts have given as good as they’ve got, if not more.

This has been a lively match, better than most run-of-the-mill pre-season friendlies. Chelsea seeing a fair bit of possession at the moment, can they fashion a chance?

Yes they can. But it’s a longish shot from Gittens that is easily saved by Hamzi in the JDT goal.

More niggle in this match that hasn’t really had many tough challenges. After a few handbags the referee takes control and the argy bargy peters out.

It’s the least the hosts deserve. They have a free-kick 25 yards out, Arribas takes it with his right it’s at the wall but in turning away from the ball Delap deflects it into the far-right corner giving Slonina no chance.

Fluky goal but the hosts have deserved their bit of luck.

Delap again with the goal, this time he goes low, but still to the keeper’s right.

Penalty for Chelsea. Gittens cuts back in the box onto his right and is clipped by the defender. Clear-cut penalty.

Half-chance for Delap on the edge of the area. He playes a one-two with Jackson before opening up his body and letting fly, the shot going well wide.

Another good chance for the hosts and it’s not shock to write that it’s come from the industry of Arribas on the right. He fires in a low cross that evades everyone in the box.

Estevao goes down in the box, it looks as though it could well be a penalty but the referee waves play on. The Brazilian is the shown a yellow card for possibly lashing out having not got the decision he wanted.

The hosts have asserted themselves well this half, in much the same way as they did in the first 45 minutes.

Another good chance for the hosts and again it’s all too easy as Zahedi is one-on-one with the keeper. The striker, however, dithers a bit too long and Slonina makes a fine save. JDT have had plenty of chances to add to their sole goal...

Chelsea have had a ragged start to this half.

Good work from JDT who keep the ball well in midfield before a throughball is played to the on-rushing Zahedi but Slonina comes out well.

They’re back under way in Johor, and there’s an early chance for Jackson who gets the ball in the box, but the ball gets stuck underneath him and he cannot get in a good attempt in on goal.

And that is the last action of an entertaining half. Chelsea started well before the hosts opened the scoring. JDT then took control of the half and should, if truth be told, have extended their lead. But Delap did well to earn the penalty that he subsequently scored and should have made it 2-1 with the last kick of the 45.

Worrying signs at the back, however, for Alonso. Will Chelsea go to four at the back after the break?

The answer to that question (see last post) was so very nearly yes...

Jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

There will be three minutes of added time. Can Chelsea head into the break with an unexpected lead?

Free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

The hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

Having won the penalty Delap fires the spotkick home, sending the keeper the the wrong way.

Penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

Chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back currently.

As I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

JDT are finding a lot of joy on the flanks, there are three at the back for Chelsea and on the outside are two youngsters. The hosts are working the space well.

Yet again Chelsea are made to look decidedly average. A simple ball over the top on the right opens up the visitors’ defence and Arribas is in on goal, he cuts in and lets fly with his left peg, the shot going wide.

That should have been 2-0 to the Malaysian powerhouses.

Worrying signs for Chelsea who have struggled to keep possession up top and looked vulnerable at the back.

Yet more good work from JDT who are being given space by Chelsea. Marcos Guilherme slaloms into the west Londoners’ box and Tosin again doesn’t look the most assured but the JDT player cuts the ball back and the visitors can clear the danger.

Another good attack from the hosts who get in a shot in on goal, it’s deflected and loops into the grateful arms of Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal.

There’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

Yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

There’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

Lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

So very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

Free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

What can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

No sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

Quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

They’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

CHELSEA XI TO FACE JOHOR: Sharman-Lowe; Sarr, Tosin, Anselmino; Quenda, Nicoll-Jazuli, Essugo (c), Gittens; Estevao; Jackson, Delap; subs: Slonina, Curd, Subuloye, Diakite, Watson, Mudryk, Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen, Satpayev

...Luis Garcia. The Spaniard has history with Chelsea, remember the ‘ghost goal’?

Arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n

Your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc

A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

Johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

#1909. Harrogate Town v Altrincham: Simon Weaver looking for his players to be ‘intense but not impatient’

Simon Weaver wants his Harrogate Town players to be “intense but not impatient” when they host Altrincham this afternoon (November 14).

The Sulphurites are among the top scorers in the National League having adopted an attack-minded approach upon their return to non-league football.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

However, as they were beaten 4-1 by AFC Fylde in the FA Cup last week, the front-footed hosts were guilty of being lax at the back.

“The structure we want to play with is go-getting,” said Weaver. “It’s exciting, it’s brought us a lot of goals this season with a new group, it’s been exhilarating at times.

“But the flip side is, you can leave yourself a little bit open if we don’t manage those situations where we’re right on top.

“Make sure the numbers are right defensively, make sure we don’t go haphazard with it and gung-ho and leave ourselves open to a counter-attack. The message is still to be intense but not impatient.”

Somewhat unsurprisingly, Weaver cut a relaxed figure as he previewed the hosting of seventh-placed Altrincham at the Marcy Fitness Stadium.

His second-placed side have evidently won his trust and Weaver has saluted their “insatiable desire” to improve.

“It’s a reaction but also just showing what we’ve worked on in training,” he said. “We keep trying to modify it and keep getting better as a group.

“They’ve been great. I think it’s less of a reaction and more maturing as a group and learning about each other. And actually not letting games run away from us when actually, we were right on top after half an hour.

“At 1-1, we’re in the driving seat, so much so that we probably got our eye off the ball in terms of the defensive set-up when the ball was in the attacking third. We just weren’t quite set up right or as solid as we might have been.

“They’ve got a real insatiable desire to improve themselves. I feel it’s an easy group to manage, there’s loads of capability within the group to dust themselves down and go again.”

#1908. Gary Neville tells Mauricio Pochettino to reject Manchester United unless two signings are made

Gary Neville has told Mauricio Pochettino to reject the Manchester United job unless the club promise to sign two defenders in the January transfer window.

With United confirming the sacking of Michael Carrick on Thursday morning, Pochettino is now expected to take over at Old Trafford.

After Sunday’s 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa, United sit 18th in the Premier League table after 10 games, while they are also out of the Carabao Cup following a defeat to Brighton in September.

Pochettino, who has a $10 million (£7.44m) release clause in his contract with the United States Soccer Federation, has already reached an agreement with United over a move to Old Trafford.

However, Neville believes the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager should turn down United unless the club’s hierarchy can issue guarantees over spending in the next two transfer windows.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘I’ve actually asked for Mauricio Pochettino to be the manager of Manchester United probably for seven or eight years and he’s finally going to get it, a bit late in the day for me but he’s finally going to get it,’ Neville said on Stick to Football.

‘He’s going to be sat in the Anfield dugout a week on Sunday, do we think that this is an appointment that will take Manchester United back to a level whereby over three or five years he can keep his job and he can deliver what Klopp did at Liverpool or what Arteta did at Arsenal where there’s that gradual improvement, that feeling you’re on a journey where something can happen?

‘If I was Mauricio Pochettino now, I would be literally protecting myself up to the high heaven. He’ll do that with a payoff, so do that in your contract.

‘But secondly, he needs two defenders in January. So he’s got to insist that he gets two defenders in January.

‘He’s got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer window to be able to turn this around. He’s got to insist that he gets a budget that follows.

‘They have to give it to him, or else he shouldn’t take the job. If you are not going to give them a look without that defence and that midfield, by the way, and that midfield has some money spent on it, he’s got to insist on the way in there’s some form of transfer control, there’s some sort of budget where he can meaningfully change the team. I think he needs to protect himself in the next 12 months with the transfer budget, he has to. The only time you can insist on it is at the very beginning.

‘Because if they have Dorgu at left-back, Mazraoui at right-back and Yoro and Heaven at centre-back, he will have to do one hell of a job coaching to get them up the league.’

Neville added: ‘The back four that he finished with on Sunday was Dalot left-back, Mazraoui right-back, Lenny Yoro and Ayden Heaven. That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League.

‘I don’t know a back four that is worse than that in the Premier League right now if I watch it. That is… I can’t believe Manchester United have ended up with that back four.’

#1906. Mauricio Pochettino will ditch four Man Utd stars – the winners and losers under new boss

Mauricio Pochettino is poised to take the reins at Manchester United in the club’s latest attempt to reset the clock.

Having been regarded as a genuine candidate for the job at Old Trafford on three occasions in the past, the Argentine now gets his chance in Manchester where United’s situation is more dire than ever.

With Michael Carrick’s exit confirmed, Pochettino will inherit a squad that has been routinely booed off the pitch by a fanbase thoroughly disenchanted with a lack of effort on it. While there may be hopes of recruitment in the January transfer window, Pochettino will have to work with what he has at his disposal until then.

Metro looks across the United squad to identify whose prospects look brighter than ever with the new manager en route – and those who face the axe.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

With Benjamin Sesko starting just two matches this season before injury struck again, Bryan Mbeumo has spent most of the campaign operating up top. He could remain in that role until Sesko is fit again but both he and Matheus Cunha stand to benefit in their natural positions under the new regime.

Pochettino has favoured inverted wingers to help create overloads in the middle with Cunha in particular tailor made for that role.

Moussa Dembele evolved into one of the Premier League’s most dominant midfielders at Tottenham under Pochettino, carrying on the work started by Martin Jol at Fulham with the Belgian. Kobbie Mainoo lacks Dembele’s outstanding athleticism but his press resistance and running power with the ball will be regarded as key assets for Pochettino.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Mainoo does not have the constant high-energy output Pochettino has traditionally demanded of his midfielders but he has improved his engine over the last two years and his ability to break the lines could also see him play a key role.

Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick all lauded the qualities of Mason Mount despite injuries ensuring they never saw the best of him. Pochettino could be another to look favourably upon him if he can prove his fitness.

When in negotiations with Chelsea back in 2023, Pochettino was eager for the club to end a contract stand-off with the midfielder and was desperate to keep him and make him a key component of his rebuild west London. His own arrival came too late to revive negotiations however with Mount joining United that summer.

Mount’s work rate has never been in doubt and his abilities to run off the ball or intelligently drop into space could be vital. But with just one start in the Premier League this season, the same old doubts are in place.

In October, former United captain Gary Neville called time on the Mainoo-Youri Tielemans partnership, neither dynamic or athletic enough to last the course in the Premier League. There may only be one winner with the Belgian perhaps most at risk.

Tielemans is adept in keeping possession and progressing play but his lack of drive up the pitch is seemingly at odds with how Pochettino likes to set up his midfield. Pochettino was also said to have turned down the chance to sign the midfielder on at least one occasion after his name was put forward by the Tottenham board.

The same concerns for Tielemans could also apply for another summer recruit in Andrey Santos who looks to be another passive operator based on evidence to date.

The emphasis Pochettino puts on his full-backs has been huge during his time in the Premier League but it is the area of the pitch where United are perhaps at their weakest. Diogo Dalot’s shortcomings on the right continue to be exposed while a long-term replacement for Luke Shaw is well overdue.

Dalot’s prospects are brighter – while his final ball is consistently short of the required standard, his ability to get up and down the pitch will be important. Shaw can no longer offer that kind of service on the left and Pochettino may favour the energy of Patrick Dorgu.

Pochettino helped nurture Shaw at Southampton before his £27million move to Manchester in 2014 but the 31-year-old will now struggle to provide the intensity the role demands.

United’s defence has been an utter mess and with the exception of perhaps Leny Yoro, all should consider their futures uncertain. But at 34, Maguire is perhaps the most at risk.

Pochettino favours a high defensive line, requiring centre-halves with pace to live with it. Maguire will turn 34 in March and has been at the heart of a backline that has conceded 19 goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Pochettino may favour the younger legs of Yoro and Ayden Heaven while Lisandro Martinez’s ability to build from the back could keep him in the picture for now.

#1905. GdS: A start vs. France at San Siro – Cisse’s rapid ascent continues with Mancini’s faith

Alphadjo Cisse continues to go from strength to strength, and his biggest moment yet might be coming during the break.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, beyond the confidence with which he plays and speaks, what’s truly striking is Cisse’s composure in front of goal at just 20 years of age, experiencing his first proper season in the top flight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His goal in Genoa seemed easy because he made it so, but it wasn’t. Adrien Rabiot’s pass was quite slow, the distance to the goal wasn’t that close, Genoa were exposed after losing the ball but Bijlow wasn’t in a particularly bad position, and beating him required precision.

Other strikers in those circumstances may have opted for a powerful finish. Not Cisse. He looked for the corner and found it with a lovely precise strike, one which revealed everything about the groove he has found himself in.

It was goal number five in the league for Alphadjo Cisse, making him Milan’s joint-top scorer alongside Rabiot. That extends to eight across all competitions, which puts the young Italian alone on the pedastal.

Two stats in particular stand out. The first: with his fifth goal in his ninth league appearance at 20 years and 17 days, he became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Pato (18 years and 181 days).

Second: he is one of only three players born in 2006 or later in the five major European leagues in 2026-27 to have scored at least eight goals in all competitions, along with Yamal (13) and Brunner (8).

Oh, and there’s another pretty good one: Shevchenko also scored eight goals in his first 13 games of the season with the Diavolo (although he achieved this in fewer minutes). The reward could well be a renewal, to fend off Premier League interest too.

🇮🇹 “The San Siro boys. Esposito plus Cissé: Mancini looks to a Milanese Italy.”

🤔 “Esposito is a lock at centre-forward, the debutant Alphadjo could join him in the attacking trio against France. Could Zaniolo be there too?” pic.twitter.com/zCkNmyqISY

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 10, 2026

Now, a change in dressing room awaits over the break. Roberto Mancini called him up to the senior national team for the first time, and according to La Gazzetta, the talent could start immediately.

He’s currently competing for a spot on the left in the 4-3-3 formation with Cambiaghi and Sebastiano Esposito. The Rossoneri guarantees more presence in the penalty area and quality in finishing, while Cambiaghi provides more coverage.

We’ll see if Mancini ultimately chooses to use him from the start, but what’s certain is that the former Verona man will be ready no matter what, and for a game at San Siro against France no less.
